tweets.text:
AI is real.

But the LLM-token economy still looks like a bubble.

The money flow is simple:

Enterprise → LLM → GPU → Memory

Investors are moving upstream in search of certainty.

No one knows which AI app will win, so they buy the LLM labs. No one knows whether OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, or xAI will win, so they buy NVIDIA. No one knows how durable GPU demand is, so they buy memory.

Every layer looks safer than the one below it. But that certainty is an illusion. The entire chain is still funded by the layer closest to real ROI.

Enterprises pay for tokens because they are trying to prove LLM adoption works. But so far, LLM productivity gains have not clearly translated into revenue growth. Consumers are not obviously buying more. Expenses are not obviously falling either.

Most AI-related layoffs look more like companies using LLMs to rationalize previous overhiring. The layoffs truly driven by “AI efficiency” often create backlash, operational problems, or quality issues. When hallucination is still unsolved, critical work still needs human supervision.

So the economics are awkward: no obvious revenue lift, no obvious expense reduction, and a new token bill on top.

Meanwhile, customers are not receiving much of the surplus. They are not getting better products at lower prices. They are getting higher prices, worse content, and weaker job security.

Personally, I hate this most when I see gaming consoles getting more expensive, PCs getting more expensive, Macs getting more expensive, and the internet filling up with lower-quality AI slop.

If consumers do not spend more, the companies selling to them cannot justify ever-growing LLM expenses. And enterprises do not need to abandon LLMs for the chain to break. They only need to slow the growth of LLM spending.
tweets.text_zh:
人工智能是真实的。

但LLM代币经济看起来仍然像一个泡沫。

资金流向很简单：

企业 → 法学硕士 → GPU → 内存

投资者正在向上游寻求确定性。

没有人知道哪一个人工智能应用程序会获胜，所以他们买下了法学硕士实验室。没有人知道 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google、Meta 或 xAI 是否会获胜，因此他们购买了 NVIDIA。没有人知道 GPU 需求有多持久，所以他们购买内存。

每一层看起来都比下面一层更安全。但这种确定性只是一种幻觉。整个链仍然由最接近真实投资回报率的层提供资金。

企业支付代币是因为他们试图证明 LLM 的采用是有效的。但到目前为止，LLM 生产率的提高尚未明显转化为收入增长。消费者显然并没有购买更多。费用也没有明显下降。

大多数与人工智能相关的裁员看起来更像是公司利用法学硕士来合理化之前的过度招聘。真正由“人工智能效率”驱动的裁员往往会产生反弹、运营问题或质量问题。当幻觉仍未解决时，关键工作仍然需要人类监督。

因此，经济状况很尴尬：没有明显的收入提升，没有明显的费用减少，而且还有新的代币账单。

与此同时，客户并没有收到太多盈余。他们没有以更低的价格获得更好的产品。他们的价格更高，内容更差，工作保障也更弱。

就我个人而言，当我看到游戏机变得越来越贵、PC 越来越贵、Mac 越来越贵、互联网上充斥着低质量的 AI 垃圾时，我最讨厌这种情况。

如果消费者不增加支出，向他们销售产品的公司就无法证明不断增加的法学硕士费用是合理的。企业不需要因为链条断裂而放弃法学硕士。他们只需要减缓法学硕士支出的增长。

This is another similar scenario. The first part is almost identical, but the second half is far more dangerous than mine.

When an event is unfolding in real time, there are multiple plausible futures with similar probabilities. FSD cannot assume the best-case outcome. In this video, the other driver actually accelerated into the lane and created an extremely dangerous situation.

What’s interesting is that FSD made almost the same magnitude of evasive maneuver in his video as it did in mine. That suggests FSD was not overreacting in my case. It was choosing a “Game theory Optimal”-style strategy: instead of betting on what the reckless human driver would do next, it positioned itself to preserve safety across multiple possible outcomes.

This is the kind of strategy humans often fail to appreciate, because humans judge the event after seeing how it ended.

tweets.text:
I gave it more thought, and I think I found all the answers. I have to say SpaceX’s story is much harder to comprehend compared with Tesla’s.

The short answer is that 1) inference is trending toward becoming the majority of future compute expense. One day, training in space might also make economic sense. 2) Sending AI chips to space does not make compute cheaper in absolute terms, but during a severe shortage, it can make adding new compute less expensive relative to ground-based alternatives. And 3) to make the AI story complete, Terafab must succeed in solving the production capacity issue around memory and packaging. Hopefully, faster iteration is the key to addressing that challenge, but the risk remains.


Raines (@raines1220)

Please correct me if I’m wrong, but here are my thoughts about AI satellite from SPCX:

1. Training/inference: They are kilometers away from each other. Due to physics limitations, the latency and bandwidth between satellites will make them better suited for inference only, not training.

2. Energy saving: Energy cost for data centers is usually less than 10%. The majority of data center cost today is still depreciation of AI chips. Therefore, even if you consider energy cost as zero, I still have trouble seeing significant cost efficiency when comparing on-ground data centers with in-space ones.

3. Production capacity: If AI chip manufacturing speed is the scaling bottleneck, then launching AI satellites does not unblock scaling, since the satellites still need to wait for the chips. Otherwise, the plan to have 10,000 Starship launches per year becomes the bottleneck, and at this speed, it still does not significantly outpace the expected compute scaling speed on the ground within five years.



— http://nitter.meowing.monster/raines1220/status/2066538753670402167#m
tweets.text_zh:
我思考了更多，我想我找到了所有的答案。不得不说，与特斯拉相比，SpaceX 的故事更难理解。

简而言之，1）推理正趋于成为未来计算支出的主要部分。有一天，太空训练也可能具有经济意义。 2）将人工智能芯片发送到太空并不会使计算绝对便宜，但在严重短缺的情况下，它可以使添加新计算相对于地面替代方案更便宜。 3) 为了使人工智能故事更加完整，Terafab 必须成功解决内存和封装方面的产能问题。希望更快的迭代是解决这一挑战的关键，但风险仍然存在。


雷恩斯（@raines1220）

如果我错了，请纠正我，但以下是我对 SPCX 人工智能卫星的看法：

1. 训练/推理：它们彼此相距数公里。由于物理限制，卫星之间的延迟和带宽将使它们更适合仅进行推理，而不是训练。

2、节能：数据中心的能源成本通常低于10%。如今数据中心成本的大部分仍然是人工智能芯片的折旧。因此，即使您认为能源成本为零，在将地面数据中心与太空数据中心进行比较时，我仍然很难看到显着的成本效率。

3.产能：如果说AI芯片的制造速度是扩容的瓶颈，那么发射AI卫星并不能畅通扩容，因为卫星还需要等待芯片。否则，每年发射 10,000 次星舰的计划将成为瓶颈，而按照这个速度，它仍然不会明显超过五年内地面预期的计算扩展速度。
